📋 Detailed Results Analysis

Revenue & Reserve Income

Circle's Q4 2025 total revenue and reserve income of $770 million surpassed the $745 million Street consensus by $25 million (+3.4%), accelerating from Q3's $740 million (+4.8% QoQ). Full-year 2025 revenue of $2.747 billion grew 64% year-over-year, driven by three compounding forces: (1) USDC supply expansion, (2) above-expectation reserve yield maintenance, and (3) early commercialization of the "Other Revenue" segment.

Reserve income of $2.637 billion in FY2025 (+59% YoY) reflects the dramatic growth in USDC in circulation from $43.8B at year-end 2024 to $75.3B at year-end 2025 (+72%). The Q4 reserve return rate of 3.81% — while down 68 basis points YoY reflecting Fed rate cuts — held firm sequentially and was materially above internal models. Distribution and transaction costs of $1.662 billion in FY2025 (+64% YoY) tracked revenue growth, keeping the RLDC margin range of 38–40% intact throughout each quarter of 2025.

Figure 1: Quarterly Revenue & Reserve Income ($M) — Q1 2024 to Q4 2025. Source: Circle press release, Feb 25, 2026

Earnings Per Share & Profitability

Adjusted EPS of $0.43 for Q4 2025 beat the $0.35 consensus by $0.08 (+22.9%), the second consecutive significant EPS beat. The drivers were threefold: stronger-than-expected RLDC margin (40% vs. ~38.5% est.), a 32% YoY increase in adjusted operating expenses — well below the 64% revenue growth rate — and a lower effective tax rate on continuing operations.

Reported net income from continuing operations of $133 million in Q4 reflects a dramatic +$129 million YoY improvement. On a full-year basis, the GAAP net loss of $70 million was entirely attributable to $424 million in stock-based compensation expense related to IPO vesting conditions (triggered by the June 2025 listing), masking underlying operating leverage. Stripping out the IPO SBC charge, normalized FY2025 net income would have been approximately $354 million.

Figure 2: Quarterly Adjusted EPS — with Q4 consensus overlay. Source: Circle press release; Zacks/Bloomberg consensus as of Feb 2026

Margin Analysis

The RLDC margin — Circle's key profitability metric representing revenue after distribution and transaction costs as a percentage of gross revenue — held at 40% in Q4, at the top end of the 38–40% guidance range and matching Q1 2025 levels. This demonstrates disciplined incentive management: while distribution costs grew 52% YoY, the prior-year Q4 included a $60 million one-time distribution fee, creating a favorable comparison. Excluding that one-time item, Q4 2025 distribution cost growth was approximately 31% YoY versus revenue growth of 77% — a notable positive operating leverage story.

Adjusted EBITDA margin of 21.7% for Q4 (and 21.2% for FY2025) reflects the still-early stage of Circle's operating cost scaling. As adjusted operating expenses ($570–585M guided for 2026) grow at a fraction of revenue growth, we model EBITDA margin expansion of 200–300 basis points in 2026.

💰 USDC Network Metrics

USDC's network metrics in Q4 and FY2025 far exceeded expectations, underscoring the flywheel dynamics that differentiate Circle from pure fintech peers:

  • Circulation: $75.3B at year-end 2025, +72% YoY — ahead of the company's 40% CAGR target. USDC minting reached $82.4B (+107% YoY) while redemptions of $80.9B (+157% YoY) reflect increasing institutional treasury management activity.
  • On-Chain Volume: Nearly $12 trillion (+247% YoY) — a figure that dwarfs the market cap of most payment networks and signals USDC's growing role as backbone infrastructure for decentralized finance and AI-agent payments.
  • Market Share: Stablecoin market share (Visa bot-adjusted) rose from 39% in Q3 to nearly 50% in Q4, an extraordinary 1,100-basis-point sequential gain driven by Tether's growing regulatory uncertainty under the GENIUS Act framework vs. Circle's proactive regulatory compliance posture.
  • Meaningful Wallets: 6.8 million meaningful wallets active (+59% YoY), indicating genuine user and institutional adoption beyond speculative holding.
  • On-Platform USDC: $12.5B in on-platform holdings (+5.6x YoY), now representing 17% of total circulation — a key monetization lever as Circle earns the full reserve yield on this tranche.

💡 Updated Investment Thesis

What Changed This Quarter

  • Stablecoin Market Share Inflection (Positive): The jump from 39% to ~50% adjusted stablecoin market share in a single quarter is the single most impactful datapoint from Q4. This appears driven by Tether's regulatory overhang under the GENIUS Act, institutional risk aversion toward non-regulated stablecoin issuers, and Circle's proactive acquisition of a conditional national trust charter in December 2025.
  • AI Agent Payment Thesis Gaining Real Traction (Positive): CEO Jeremy Allaire's assertion that 99% of agentic payments currently utilize USDC is a bold and, if accurate, transformative data point. Circle's incumbent position as the dominant dollar-denominated settlement layer positions it for a secular growth opportunity the market is only beginning to price.
  • IPO SBC Overhang Clearing (Neutral-to-Positive): The $424M SBC charge from IPO vesting conditions that depressed FY2025 GAAP earnings is a one-time item. FY2026 will be the first clean year of GAAP profitability, which we expect to unlock additional institutional ownership and index inclusion.
  • Distribution Cost Discipline (Positive): Despite adding major institutional partners (JPMorgan, Mastercard, Intuit, Cash App), Q4 distribution costs of $461M grew only 52% YoY while revenue grew 77%. This gap — the RLDC margin remaining at 40% — suggests new partnerships are increasingly being added on more favorable economic terms.
  • Arc and CPN in Optionality Zone (Not Yet in Price): The Arc Layer-1 blockchain and Circle Payments Network represent optionality not in our base case. CPN's $5.7B annualized volume and 55 enrolled institutions barely register on a $2.7B revenue base, but the growth trajectory (68% sequential volume increase, 74 more institutions under review) suggests these could be material contributors by late 2026/2027.

Key Risks to Thesis

  • Interest Rate Risk High — Circle's reserve income is directly tied to short-term rates. A 100bp decline in SOFR reduces FY2026E revenue by ~$750M assuming a $75B average USDC balance. Each Fed cut represents a direct headwind; consensus currently prices 2 cuts in 2026.
  • Competition from USDT and New Entrants Medium — Tether retains a $100B+ circulation base and continues to gain adoption in emerging markets. PayPal USD, Ripple's RLUSD, and bank-issued stablecoins under the GENIUS Act framework represent longer-term competitive risks.
  • Regulatory Risk Low-Med — Circle is the primary beneficiary of U.S. stablecoin regulation. However, the GENIUS Act is still being finalized, and any unexpected provision could alter the competitive landscape.
  • Execution Risk on Arc and CPN Medium — Neither Arc nor CPN has demonstrated material revenue contribution. Mainnet launch delays or institutional adoption slower than projected could weigh on the growth premium embedded in valuation.
  • USDC Depegging Event Tail Risk — A repeat of the March 2023 SVB-driven USDC depeg — though Circle now holds 100% of reserves in T-bills and overnight repos — remains a tail risk event that could trigger rapid institutional redemptions and permanent market share loss.

Catalysts

  • Arc mainnet launch (targeted 2026) — could unlock new transaction fee revenue
  • GENIUS Act finalization — provides legal clarity driving institutional USDC adoption
  • CLARITY Act passage — anticipated unlock for capital markets USDC usage
  • CPN reaching $25B+ annualized volume — demonstrates meaningful revenue diversification
  • First national digital currency bank charter approval (conditional approval received Dec 2025)
  • EURC crossing €1B circulation — demonstrates non-USD growth optionality
  • S&P 500 index inclusion (possible as GAAP profitability achieved in FY2026)
💲 Valuation & Updated Estimates

Revised Price Target: $110 (From $90)

We raise our 12-month price target to $110 from $90, reflecting: (1) higher FY2026E RLDC estimates following the Q4 beat and margin outperformance, (2) a higher warranted multiple given the stablecoin market share inflection and AI-agent payment optionality, and (3) clearing of the IPO SBC overhang that suppressed GAAP earnings in FY2025. At $110, CRCL trades at approximately 33x FY2026E RLDC of $1.29B and approximately 32x FY2026E Adj. EBITDA of $710M.

Our valuation framework employs a blended methodology: (1) EV/RLDC multiple comparison to stablecoin and crypto infrastructure peers, (2) a discounted cash flow model using a 5-year explicit forecast period with an 18% discount rate and 4% terminal growth rate, and (3) an EV/EBITDA multiple-of-peers analysis. The blended result suggests a fair value range of $95–125, with $110 as our central estimate.
